hints: Use a separate partial-fraction term for each power of the repeated factor $3-x$.
Write $f(x)=\dfrac A{x+2}+\dfrac B{3-x}+\dfrac C{(3-x)^2}$ and clear the denominator.
Substitute $x=-2$ and $x=3$ to determine two constants, then compare a coefficient or use another convenient value for the third.
walkthrough:
Set up the partial fraction decomposition for the rational function with repeated linear factor $(3 - x)^2$:
$$\dfrac{16 - 17x}{(2 + x)(3 - x)^2} = \dfrac{A}{2 + x} + \dfrac{B}{3 - x} + \dfrac{C}{(3 - x)^2}$$

Multiply both sides by $(2 + x)(3 - x)^2$ to form the algebraic identity:
$$16 - 17x = A(3 - x)^2 + B(2 + x)(3 - x) + C(2 + x)$$

Substitute $x = 3$ to isolate $C$:
$$\text{LHS} = 16 - 17(3) = 16 - 51 = -35$$
$$\text{RHS} = A(0) + B(0) + C(2 + 3) = 5C$$
$$5C = -35 \implies C = -7$$

Equate coefficients of $x^2$ to find $B$:
On the LHS, the coefficient of $x^2$ is $0$.
On the RHS, $A(3 - x)^2 = A(x^2 - 6x + 9)$ contributes $Ax^2$, and $B(2 + x)(3 - x) = B(-x^2 + x + 6)$ contributes $-Bx^2$.
$$A - B = 0 \implies B = A = 2$$

Verify by substituting $x = 0$:
$$\text{LHS} = 16$$
$$\text{RHS} = A(9) + B(6) + C(2) = 2(9) + 2(6) + (-7)(2) = 18 + 12 - 14 = 16 \quad \text{(verified)}$$

Write the final partial fractions expression:
$$\mathrm{f}(x) = \dfrac{2}{2 + x} + \dfrac{2}{3 - x} - \dfrac{7}{(3 - x)^2}$$

hints: Use the partial fractions from part (i) and expand each factor about $x=0$.
Rewrite the denominators as multiples of $(1+x/2)$ and $(1-x/3)$; the repeated factor uses $(1-x/3)^{-2}$.
Multiply by the partial-fraction coefficients, retain terms through $x^2$, and combine like powers.
walkthrough:
Write the partial fractions using negative exponents:
$$\mathrm{f}(x) = 2(2 + x)^{-1} + 2(3 - x)^{-1} - 7(3 - x)^{-2}$$

Expand the first term $2(2 + x)^{-1}$:
$$2(2 + x)^{-1} = 2\left[2\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)\right]^{-1} = 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{-1} = \left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{-1}$$
Apply the binomial series $(1 + u)^{-1} = 1 - u + u^2 - \dots$ with $u = \dfrac{x}{2}$:
$$\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^{-1} = 1 - \dfrac{x}{2} + \left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2 = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{1}{4}x^2$$

Expand the second term $2(3 - x)^{-1}$:
$$2(3 - x)^{-1} = 2\left[3\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)\right]^{-1} = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{-1}$$
Apply the binomial series $(1 - u)^{-1} = 1 + u + u^2 + \dots$ with $u = \dfrac{x}{3}$:
$$\dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{3} + \left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)^2\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{3}x + \dfrac{1}{9}x^2\right) = \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{9}x + \dfrac{2}{27}x^2$$

Expand the third term $-7(3 - x)^{-2}$:
$$-7(3 - x)^{-2} = -7\left[3\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)\right]^{-2} = -7 \cdot 3^{-2}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{-2} = -\dfrac{7}{9}\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{-2}$$
Apply the binomial series $(1 - u)^{-2} = 1 + 2u + 3u^2 + \dots$ with $u = \dfrac{x}{3}$:
$$\left(1 - \dfrac{x}{3}\right)^{-2} = 1 + 2\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right) + 3\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)^2 = 1 + \dfrac{2}{3}x + 3\left(\dfrac{x^2}{9}\right) = 1 + \dfrac{2}{3}x + \dfrac{1}{3}x^2$$
Multiply by $-\dfrac{7}{9}$:
$$-\dfrac{7}{9}\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3}x + \dfrac{1}{3}x^2\right) = -\dfrac{7}{9} - \dfrac{14}{27}x - \dfrac{7}{27}x^2$$

Combine coefficients:
- Constant term:
$$1 + \dfrac{2}{3} - \dfrac{7}{9} = \dfrac{9 + 6 - 7}{9} = \dfrac{8}{9}$$
- Coefficient of $x$:
$$-\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{2}{9} - \dfrac{14}{27} = -\dfrac{27}{54} + \dfrac{12}{54} - \dfrac{28}{54} = \dfrac{-27 + 12 - 28}{54} = -\dfrac{43}{54}$$
- Coefficient of $x^2$:
$$\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{2}{27} - \dfrac{7}{27} = \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{5}{27} = \dfrac{27 - 20}{108} = \dfrac{7}{108}$$
